editorial:
Ever wonder what happens behind the scenes at a legendary animation studio? You get to hang out with Walt Disney himself as he plays around with some cool studio props and shows off a few magic tricks. It feels like you are just hanging out in his office. Once the live-action part wraps up, a funny character called the Slave in the Magic Mirror takes over. He acts as your guide through a series of classic magic-themed cartoons that show off the creativity of the studio. The whole thing has a cozy, old-school vibe that makes you feel like you are watching a special presentation from a bygone era.

What really makes this work is the pacing; it never feels too long because the cartoons keep things moving quickly. The animation is bright and charming, though some of the jokes are very dated. If you love Disney history or just want something light to watch with the family, you will love this. Since it is a vintage piece, you should look for it in a high-quality restored version. You can try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see those colors pop. If you are a real collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up after the Slave in the Magic Mirror finishes showing the curated collection of magic cartoons. He gives a final funny farewell to the audience, reminding you that the real magic is the imagination used to create these films. There is no big plot twist since it is a documentary, but it ends on a high note by bringing the focus back to the joy of animation and Walt's vision.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Disney history and classic animation.
